title: The Slave Trade Act 1807
summary: An act of the United Kingdom Parliament prohibiting the Atlantic slave trade throughout the British Empire, in force from 1 May 1807 after eighteen years of failed bills. It freed nobody: slavery remained legal in most of the empire until the Slavery Abolition Act of 1833. What it did beyond British ships was to turn abolition into British foreign policy — the cited article says it encouraged British action to press other states to abolish their own trades — and that pressure is what the Brazilian half of this milestone spends the next forty years under.

actors.note: an act of its Parliament, in force from 1 May 1807 throughout the British Empire
